title: Localized coefficient-ring counit criterion for forgetting module lower shriek
statement:
Fix the small-site universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a continuous and cocontinuous functor of sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1), let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal D$, and put $R'=R\circ u$ with identity structural ring map. Write $T:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R')$ and $T^{\mathrm{Ab}}:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ for precomposition, and $F_{\mathcal C},F_{\mathcal D}$ for forgetting module actions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Fix an additive left adjoint $L\dashv T$, with unit $\eta$, and a left adjoint $A\dashv T^{\mathrm{Ab}}$. For every $U\in\mathcal C$ let $u_U:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal D/u(U)$ be the induced continuous and cocontinuous functor on localized sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], let $T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}$ be its precomposition functor on abelian sheaves, and fix a left adjoint $A_U\dashv T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}$ with counit $\varepsilon_U$. Here an adjunction means natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(LX,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(X,TY)$, and similarly for $A,A_U$. Regard ring sheaves as abelian sheaves when applying $A_U$. Define $c_U$ to be the counit map
$$c_U:A_U(R'|_U)=A_UT_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}(R|_{u(U)})\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{U,R|_{u(U)}}}R|_{u(U)}.$$
If every $c_U$ is an isomorphism, then the natural transformation
$$\gamma:A F_{\mathcal C}\longrightarrow F_{\mathcal D}L,$$
whose component at $M$ is the $A\dashv T^{\mathrm{Ab}}$ adjunct of $F_{\mathcal C}(\eta_M):F_{\mathcal C}M\to T^{\mathrm{Ab}}F_{\mathcal D}LM$, is an isomorphism. No equivalence assumption on $u_U$, no preservation of equalizers, and no terminal object is required.

source.place: Tag 0798, remark-when-shriek-equal, natural transformation and equation-compare-on-localizations; the ring map there is the counit at the restricted ring for the identity structural map.

proof.text: Write $J_U$ for module extension by zero from $\mathcal C/U$ and $J_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}$ for abelian extension by zero; use the same notation on $\mathcal D$. Their adjunctions with restriction are [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf-adjoint]. Both constructions have the same underlying presheaf: its value at $V$ is the sum of the groups $H(V\xrightarrow a U)$ over arrows $a:V\to U$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Module sheafification has underlying abelian sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Thus $FJ_UH=J_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}FH$, with the identifications preserving the inclusions of the summands. In particular, for $E_U=J_U(R'|_U)$ and $Q_U=J_{u(U)}(R|_{u(U)})$, we have $F_{\mathcal C}E_U=J_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}(R'|_U)$ and $F_{\mathcal D}Q_U=J_{u(U)}^{\mathrm{Ab}}(R|_{u(U)})$. These are the sheafified free representables of [lem-trf-ringed-site-restriction-generator-data], by their identical sum formulas.

For every $R$-module sheaf $N$, adjunction and the evaluation bijections of [lem-trf-ringed-site-restriction-generator-data] give natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_R(LE_U,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}(E_U,TN)\cong N(u(U))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q_U,N)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection], applied to the inverse bijection, there is an isomorphism $e_U:LE_U\to Q_U$ characterized by this correspondence. More explicitly its $L\dashv T$ adjunct $b_U:E_U\to TQ_U$ corresponds to the standard section $e_{1_{u(U)}}\in Q_U(u(U))$. Consequently $b_U=T(e_U)\eta_{E_U}$. On the presheaf summand indexed by $a:V\to U$, it sends $r\in R'(V)=R(u(V))$ to $r e_{u(a)}\in Q_U(u(V))$, followed by sheafification.

source.place: Tag 0797, lemma-lower-shriek-modules, evaluation calculation; Categories Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda, on the opposite category.

proof.text:
Put $B=R|_{u(U)}$ and $S=R'|_U=T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}B$, considered as abelian sheaves. For any abelian sheaf $N$ on $\mathcal D$, the two localization adjunctions [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf-adjoint] and the adjunctions in the hypotheses give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(AJ_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}S,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(S,(T^{\mathrm{Ab}}N)|_U)=\operatorname{Hom}(S,T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}(N|_{u(U)}))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A_US,N|_{u(U)})\cong\operatorname{Hom}(J_{u(U)}^{\mathrm{Ab}}A_US,N).$$
The middle equality is sectionwise: both restrictions at $V\to U$ are $N(u(V))$, with the same maps [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The bijections are natural in $N$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] to their inverse defines an isomorphism $\lambda_U:AJ_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}S\to J_{u(U)}^{\mathrm{Ab}}A_US$. This specifies its normalization, including the units; no base-change theorem is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0798, remark-when-shriek-equal, identity g_!^{Ab} j_{U!}=j_{u(U)!}(g\prime)_!^{Ab}; Tag 03DI localization adjunction.

proof.text:
We identify the actual map, not just its source and target. Let $d_U:B\to(F_{\mathcal D}Q_U)|_{u(U)}$ be the abelian localization unit, and put $\beta_U=J_{u(U)}^{\mathrm{Ab}}(c_U)\lambda_U:AF_{\mathcal C}E_U\to F_{\mathcal D}Q_U$. In the Hom chain of step 3, this map corresponds to the slice map
$$S\xrightarrow{\eta^U_S}T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}A_US\xrightarrow{T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}c_U}T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}B\xrightarrow{T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}d_U}T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}((F_{\mathcal D}Q_U)|_{u(U)}),$$
where $\eta^U$ is the unit of $A_U\dashv T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}$. Since $S=T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}B$ and $c_U=\varepsilon_{U,B}$, the first two arrows compose to $1_S$ by the triangle identity (equivalently, the counit is the adjunct of $1_{T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}B}$). The resulting map is $T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}d_U$. Under the localization adjunction its map on the summand $a:V\to U$ sends $r$ to $r e_{u(a)}$. Indeed, by the explicit adjunct formula of [lem-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf-adjoint] applied on $\mathcal D$ to the identity of $J_{u(U)}^{\mathrm{Ab}}B$, the unit $d_U$ sends $r\in B(u(V)\xrightarrow{u(a)}u(U))=R(u(V))$ to the image of $r$ in the summand of $u(a)$ of the direct-sum presheaf [def-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf], that is to $re_{u(a)}$; by the same formula applied on $\mathcal C$, the map $J_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}S\to T^{\mathrm{Ab}}F_{\mathcal D}Q_U$ corresponding to $T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}d_U$ sends $r$ in the summand of $a$ to $(T_U^{\mathrm{Ab}}d_U)_{(V,a)}(r)=re_{u(a)}$. By step 2 this is precisely $F_{\mathcal C}b_U$. Meanwhile the $A\dashv T^{\mathrm{Ab}}$ adjunct of $F_{\mathcal D}(e_U)\gamma_{E_U}$ is $T^{\mathrm{Ab}}F_{\mathcal D}(e_U)F_{\mathcal C}(\eta_{E_U})=F_{\mathcal C}b_U$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $F_{\mathcal D}(e_U)\gamma_{E_U}=\beta_U$.

source.place: Tag 0798, remark-when-shriek-equal, equation-compare-on-localizations; Tag 03DI, proof of lemma-extension-by-zero, explicit adjunction maps.

proof.text: The hypothesis makes $c_U$ invertible. The functor $J_{u(U)}^{\mathrm{Ab}}$ sends its inverse to an inverse, so $\beta_U=J_{u(U)}^{\mathrm{Ab}}(c_U)\lambda_U$ is invertible. The same holds for $F_{\mathcal D}(e_U)$. Step 4 therefore gives $\gamma_{E_U}=F_{\mathcal D}(e_U)^{-1}\beta_U$, an isomorphism for every $U$. This uses only the stated counits and does not require the slice functor to be an equivalence.

Put $P=AF_{\mathcal C}$ and $Q=F_{\mathcal D}L$. The forgetful functors preserve small coproducts and cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]; small-site sheafification exists in the fixed universes. A left adjoint preserves these colimits directly from the Hom universal property: maps out of its value on a colimit are maps from that colimit into the right adjoint, hence compatible families of maps into the right adjoint, hence compatible families of maps out of the images. Apply this to $A$ and $L$. They also preserve the initial zero object, so cokernels can be treated as coequalizers with zero. Thus $P,Q$ preserve coproducts and cokernels. Naturality of $\gamma$ follows by applying the adjunction bijection to the naturality equation for $\eta$. For a small sum $H=\bigoplus_iE_{U_i}$, naturality at every coproduct inclusion says that $\gamma_H$, under the colimit identifications, is the sum of the $\gamma_{E_{U_i}}$. Its inverse is the sum of their inverses. The empty sum is included.

source.place: Tags 03DA, lemma-abelian; 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits; 0798, reduction to the free-module generators.

proof.text: For any $M$, [lem-trf-ringed-site-restriction-generator-data] supplies a small sum $H_0$ of the $E_U$ and an epimorphism $p:H_0\to M$. Its kernel $K$ exists in the abelian module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply the same generator statement to $K$ to obtain an epimorphism $q:H_1\to K$ from another small sum, and put $a:H_1\xrightarrow qK\hookrightarrow H_0$. Then $p$ is the cokernel of $a$: a map killing $a$ kills $K$ because $q$ is epi, and therefore factors uniquely through the quotient $H_0/K=M$. Steps 5 and 6 make $\gamma_{H_0}$ and $\gamma_{H_1}$ invertible. Naturality gives a commuting square between $Pa$ and $Qa$. Their cokernels are $PM$ and $QM$ by step 6; the two inverse vertical isomorphisms also commute with the arrows and hence induce an inverse between these cokernels. The induced forward map is $\gamma_M$, by naturality at $p$ and uniqueness in the cokernel property. Thus $\gamma_M$ is invertible for every $M$, proving the asserted natural isomorphism. No projectivity of the generators was used.
